form.name: Oil and Gas Permit to Drill or Modify Well Application
form.notes: NOT READ. dnr.mo.gov answered HTTP 403 to the one request made to the permit page (not retried), and www.sos.mo.gov answered 403 for the rule 10 CSR 50-2. A third-party copy (templateroller) shows only title, release date 2018-03-01 and no fields. Every cell that depends on the form is therefore unknown; cells marked data come from the DNR's map layer and its metadata.

sources.name: Oil and Gas Wells (MoDNR/MGS viewing service, non-confidential permitted wells)
sources.license: no restriction listed (access constraints: none); no-warranty use statement; JSON, GeoJSON and PBF query formats
sources.tested: gis.dnr.mo.gov: layer ?f=pjson 200, 9 KB schema (Map, Query, Data; maxRecordCount 2000); statistics query 200: 10,369 wells, 5,307 with PERMIT_DAT (1966-05-22 to 2019-08-15), 3,940 with SPUD_DATE (newest 2021-06-04), newest STATUSDATE 2021-08-03; counts of permits dated 2015 or later: 58, dated 2019 or later: 2; distinct WELL_TYPE (16) and STATUS (15) values 200. Metadata XML (info.mo.gov, 200) says data current to 2021-08-25, update 'as needed', excludes wells under confidentiality. The layer is frozen: no permit after 2019-08.

sources.name: GeoSTRAT (MGS web map used to locate permitted oil and gas wells)
sources.tested: Named in a search summary of the DNR oil and gas pages only; the URL is the agency oil and gas page that surfaced, not the viewer; not opened, so whether it is fresher than the layer is unknown.

grade_reason: The wells layer is shaped like an A (free ArcGIS API, API number, PERMIT_DAT issue date, SPUD_DATE, well type, status, location) but it is frozen: the newest permit is 2019-08-15 and the newest spud 2021-06-04, and confidential wells are left out, so it gives history, not current monthly counts. No current bulk source or permit list was found, the permit form could not be read, and the DNR and Secretary of State pages answered 403 from here. History only: about 13 permits a year since 2015, 2 in 2019.
producer_plan: Missouri is tiny and not worth a monthly producer on the present data. A history-only file could be built from the layer (query PERMIT_DAT, SPUD_DATE, WELL_TYPE, STATUS, COUNTY; 10,369 rows fit in 6 pages of 2,000) giving permits and spuds by month through Aug 2019 / Jun 2021, and shown as 'not updated since 2021'. For current activity the owner would need a public-records request to the Geological Survey in Rolla, or to find whether GeoSTRAT or the DNR permit page publishes a fresher list (not checked: pages blocked or not opened). PERMIT_DAT covers drill, deepen and recomplete permits together, so work types cannot be separated.
privacy_notes: The layer's OPERATOR and LEASE columns may name individuals or landowners; the linked permit files and the metadata hold staff contact details (not copied). Publish only corporate, LLC or LP operator names and county-level counts.
